slides.title: Field Reports Full of Almost-Insights
bullets: Most failures are not silence but noise that looks like insight
These get logged and clutter systems without informing any decision
Recognising what is not an insight is as valuable as knowing what is

slides.title: A Raw Observation Is Not an Insight
bullets: A noted observation is real and worth keeping, but incomplete
It does not yet explain why or point to an implication
Ask whether it is a genuine trend or an artifact of one referral pattern

slides.title: A Restated Fact Adds No Understanding
bullets: Confirming a known label or literature fact is not insight
Genuine insight requires new understanding, not confirmation
If the organisation already knew it, logging it changes nothing

slides.title: An Ungrounded Opinion Isn't Actionable
bullets: A subjective impression alone gives the organisation nothing to act on
What matters is why the physician feels that way
Without the reason behind it, an opinion cannot inform a decision

slides.title: One Anecdote Is Not Yet a Trend
bullets: A single unusual case is worth noting and watching for corroboration
Treating it as representative risks steering strategy on noise
This is the same bias risk covered later in bias avoidance

slides.title: A Wish or Request Isn't an Insight
bullets: Requests for samples or programs are legitimate field feedback
They should be routed to the right owner, not logged as insight
They don't explain a why behind clinical behaviour

slides.title: One Question Before Logging Anything
bullets: Can I state in one sentence what decision this could inform, and why
If the answer is no, it is raw material, not a finished insight
Raw material is still worth keeping for later

takeaway.title: Most field notes are almost-insights until they explain a why and an action
bullets: Observations, restated facts, opinions, anecdotes and requests aren't insights alone
Each needs development before it can inform a decision
Apply the one-sentence test before logging anything as insight
